facts.text: Ladson was named after the Ladson family, one of Charleston’s oldest planter and merchant lineages, with a member who served as lieutenant governor.
French Huguenot settlers built a chapel in the early 1700s, marking the first European presence in what would become Ladson.
The South Carolina Canal and Railroad Company’s early 1830s line ran through Ladson, making it one of the first towns connected by the world’s longest continuous railroad at the time.
The community evolved from a rural area into a bedroom suburb, drawing families who wanted affordable homes near Charleston’s job market.
Ladson’s Exchange Park hosts large events that attract crowds from all three counties, becoming a regional gathering spot.
Each October, the Coastal Carolina Fair takes place in Ladson, drawing visitors for its long‑standing tradition of rides, food, and entertainment.
